From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Autumnly renewal: benchmark window + proposed save matrix

Alex —

Quick note to get ahead of your contract that comes up in mid-August: we know you're running a bakeoff with another vendor and want to make the renewal as low-friction
as possible. To surface any performance or cost gaps quickly, we propose a two-phase
benchmark handoff: a short 3-day quick-smoke followed by a 10-day production-like
validation with your real traffic routing.

What we will provide:
- Dedicated test pool (identical GPU class) for the trial window, isolated from other tenants.
- Prefix caching preserved for the production-like phase to match token-costs.
- A short save matrix that ties discounting/credits to success gates (attached: redwood-save-matrix.xlsx).

We want to validate these key metrics during the production-like run:
- 99th percentile response latency under your p95 request distribution
- Throughput (tokens/sec) at your expected peak concurrency
- Quality pass rate on your annotated prompt-set (we can run a small eval)
- Effective cost per 1M tokens with the caching/batching settings you use

Attachments: benchmark-setup-instructions.pdf (test harness, endpoints, data handling), redwood-save-matrix.xlsx (commercial anchor + rollback triggers).

If this sounds reasonable I'll ask Marissa to coordinate schedule and Karthik to confirm capacity sizing. We can offer a retention bridge (15% one-time credit + temporary price protection) while the trial is underway, contingent on the results.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow to lock the dates.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks for the clear plan. Autumnly is keen to move quickly; we're under a bit of time pressure from execs to show a technical delta. Two notes from our side:

1) Could we start with a faster 3-day bakeoff (smoke tests + latency/throughput readout) to surface any immediate gaps, then extend to the longer window if we're happy?
2) Security: procurement (Jonathan) will need details on data retention, VPC options, and SOC2 evidence before we commit any traffic. Can you confirm whether the quick-smoke can run inside a customer VPC or private deployment to avoid data egress concerns?

Also, we'd like something written up we can show execs — a one-page comparison vs. the vendor we're running in parallel (NovaServe). Can you pull a short technical/commercial side-by-side we can use in the bakeoff readout?

If you can do a quick call today at 3pm PT, we'll have Jonathan on for requirements.

Best,
